title: Building the Nest band and the opening night
summary: He assembles two saxophones, two trumpets and full rhythm, rehearses at home, and at opening the audience applauds instead of dancing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: So anyhow, I started to get a band together. Now, I wasn't trying for sound, I was trying to get a band together to eat and make a living. But, by picking, by looking at the place, I said, well you certainly don't want no trombone in there. And you don't want too big a -- but yet, I had in mind to have a round sound, but without expecting anything out of it. Because I think I was the first one in Harlem to try anything like this. So I had two saxophones, two trumpets, and a full rhythm section. But, of course, I know, if you've got a full rhythm section, it can sound like a big band, you'll get a big band sound.

You see, sometimes when you are short on one side, like if you're short in the reeds, you can take a trumpet and give him the third saxophone part, or sometime when you're short -- or when you need two trumpets and a trombone, then the tenor saxophone will answer the purpose for the general Public that don't really understand the sounds. So I put this TUBE TRIP together and I wasn't sure of it myself, so I used to rehearse at my house. And Johnny and them were beginning to get nervous. They said, "When you coming down here to rehearse?" And I said, "I'm not. I'm rehearsing up here quietly by myself and I don't want anybody to hear it." And on account of the confidence that they had in me from Baron Wilkins' place, and I'd had a nice pretty

band, they said, 'Well, we'll let you go. But you'd better be ready when you come in here, or out you go on your nose.' See, so anyhow, we opened up. And the time come and we opened up with this band, and the first note we hit, we thought it was good. But nobody danced. Well, I was scared to death. I thought it was because they didn't like it. Well, this was the beginning of concert, and I didn't realize that. For jazz bands. Then we went through the whole set. And everybody, when we got through playing, then they give us applause, and a couple of guys come up and shake your hand and say, 'Man, you've got a good sound there.'
